paragraphs.title: David’s Preparations and the Offering for the Temple

easy.explanation: David said that Solomon his son was the one whom God had chosen.
easy.q: Who was David’s son chosen by God to build the temple?

easy.explanation: David called upon all the congregation to offer willingly.
easy.q: Who did David ask to offer willingly for the work of God’s house?

easy.explanation: The people rejoiced because they offered willingly with a perfect heart.
easy.q: How did the people respond to their offering?

answers: Because the palace was for the LORD, not for man
Because there were no building materials
Because the people refused to help
medium.explanation: David said, “the palace is not for man, but for the LORD God.”
medium.q: Why did David say that the work was great?

medium.explanation: David gave gold and silver from his “own proper good.”
medium.q: What word describes David’s personal treasure of gold and silver?

answers: They offered gifts for God’s house
medium.explanation: The leaders and officers offered willingly and gave for the service of God’s house.
medium.q: What did the leaders do after David called for willing offerings?

answers: A great task may be given to a young leader
Solomon would not help build it
challenge.explanation: Solomon was young and tender, yet the work of building the palace was great.
challenge.q: What does the contrast between Solomon’s youth and the greatness of the work suggest?

answers: The extent of the preparations for the Temple
challenge.explanation: David prepared gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, and many precious stones.
challenge.q: What does David’s long list of materials emphasize?

answers: They rejoiced because they offered willingly
They rejoiced because they gave nothing
They rejoiced only because of a feast
challenge.explanation: The people rejoiced because they offered willingly with a perfect heart.
challenge.q: What connection does the passage make between the people’s offering and their joy?

paragraphs.title: David’s Blessing: Everything Comes from the Lord

easy.explanation: David blessed the LORD before all the congregation.
easy.q: Whom did David bless before all the congregation?

easy.explanation: David declared, “Thine, O LORD, is the greatness, and the power, and the glory.”
easy.q: To whom do greatness, power, and glory belong?

easy.explanation: David said, “all things come of thee, and of thine own have we given thee.”
easy.q: Where did David say that all things came from?

answers: Because they show that man is independent
Because they come from the LORD, who reigns over all
Because they belong only to the king
medium.explanation: David said that riches and honour come from the LORD, who reigns over all.
medium.q: Why did David thank the LORD for riches and honour?

medium.explanation: David described people as strangers and sojourners whose days pass away.
medium.q: What does the word “sojourners” mean in this passage?

answers: They achieved it entirely by themselves
They received everything from another king
Their ability and possessions came from the LORD
medium.explanation: David emphasized that all they had came from God’s hand.
medium.q: How did David explain the people’s ability to offer willingly?

answers: Life passes quickly and is not permanent
challenge.explanation: A shadow pictures the fleeting and temporary nature of human life.
challenge.q: What does the image of earthly days being “as a shadow” mean?

answers: As an offering made with an upright heart
challenge.explanation: David said, “in the uprightness of mine heart I have willingly offered.”
challenge.q: How did David describe his own offering?

answers: Man is the source of wealth
All wealth and power belong to and come from the LORD
The king is greater than the LORD
challenge.explanation: David repeatedly says that greatness, power, and possessions come from God.
challenge.q: What central idea appears throughout David’s blessing and thanksgiving?

paragraphs.title: A Prayer for the People and Solomon

easy.explanation: David asked God to keep the people’s hearts prepared and directed toward Him.
easy.q: What did David ask God to preserve in the people’s hearts?

easy.explanation: David asked God to give Solomon his son “a perfect heart.”
easy.q: What did David ask God to give Solomon?

answers: To keep God’s commandments and build the palace
To lead an army into battle
easy.explanation: David asked Solomon to keep God’s commandments and build the palace.
easy.q: Why did Solomon need a perfect heart?

answers: Both concern hearts directed toward serving God
medium.explanation: David prayed for faithful and prepared hearts in both the people and Solomon.
medium.q: What connection is there between David’s prayers for the people and for Solomon?

answers: A sincere and complete heart in serving God
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to wholehearted obedience to God’s commandments.
medium.q: What does “a perfect heart” mean in this context?

answers: Solomon needed both faithfulness to God and completion of the Temple
medium.explanation: Solomon was to keep God’s commandments and complete the work David had prepared.
medium.q: Why did David mention building the palace together with keeping the commandments?

answers: A single act is enough, with no need for continued faithfulness
A willing spirit should be preserved over time
Willingness has nothing to do with the heart
challenge.explanation: David asked God to keep the people’s hearts prepared and directed toward Him.
challenge.q: What does David’s prayer teach about the importance of willingness?

answers: He wanted their hearts and motives to remain faithful
He wanted to cancel their gifts
challenge.explanation: David prayed that their inward devotion would continue along with their outward gifts.
challenge.q: Why did David pray after the people had already offered?

answers: David prepared, and Solomon was to complete the building
Solomon prepared, while David only watched
challenge.explanation: David made provision, and Solomon was to build the palace.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between David’s preparation and Solomon’s role?

easy.explanation: The congregation blessed the LORD, bowed down, and worshipped Him and the king.
easy.q: What did the congregation do after David told them to bless the LORD?

easy.explanation: Solomon was made king the second time before all Israel.
easy.q: Who was made king the second time before all Israel?

easy.explanation: Zadok was appointed and anointed to be priest.
easy.q: Who was anointed to be priest?

answers: They offered sacrifices and burnt offerings
medium.explanation: On the following day they sacrificed and offered burnt offerings unto the LORD.
medium.q: What did the people do on the day after the assembly?

answers: They ate and drank before the LORD with great gladness
medium.explanation: They ate and drank before the LORD with great gladness.
medium.q: What did the people do after offering the sacrifices?

answers: All Israel obeyed him, and the leaders submitted to him
medium.explanation: All Israel obeyed Solomon, and the princes, mighty men, and David’s sons submitted to him.
medium.q: What change in leadership is described after Solomon became king?

answers: Worship included reverence, offering, and public rejoicing
The people cared only about celebration
challenge.explanation: The passage joins bowing and worship with sacrifices and joyful fellowship.
challenge.q: What does the combination of worship, sacrifices, and joy show?

answers: His leadership received renewed public recognition
He had no connection with David
challenge.explanation: The public ceremony confirmed Solomon’s rule before all Israel.
challenge.q: What does Solomon’s second coronation before all Israel indicate?

answers: All Israel obeyed him and the LORD greatly magnified him
challenge.explanation: Solomon prospered, all Israel obeyed him, and the LORD magnified him greatly.
challenge.q: How is Solomon’s success described after he sat on David’s throne?

easy.explanation: The passage says that David reigned over all Israel.
David reigned over Israel for forty years.
easy.q: How long did David reign over Israel?

easy.explanation: Solomon his son reigned in David’s stead.

medium.explanation: David reigned seven years in Hebron.
medium.q: How long did David reign in Hebron?

medium.explanation: David reigned thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
medium.q: How long did David reign in Jerusalem?

answers: In a good old age, full of days, riches, and honour
medium.explanation: The passage says David died in a good old age, full of days, riches, and honour.
medium.q: How is David described at the time of his death?

answers: After forty years, Solomon succeeded David
David and Solomon ruled together for seven years
challenge.explanation: The passage summarizes David’s forty-year reign and then states that Solomon succeeded him.
challenge.q: How does the summary of David’s reign lead to Solomon’s succession?

answers: David’s reign had two distinct periods and centers
Hebron and Jerusalem refer to the same period
challenge.explanation: The text separately records seven years in Hebron and thirty-three in Jerusalem.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the separate periods in Hebron and Jerusalem?

answers: A good old age, riches, and honour
challenge.explanation: David died in a good old age and was full of days, riches, and honour.
challenge.q: Which description presents David’s life as ending honorably?

paragraphs.title: Sources for the Account of David

easy.explanation: The passage names Samuel the seer, Nathan the prophet, and Gad the seer.
easy.q: In whose writings were the acts of David recorded?

answers: Only the building of the Temple
easy.explanation: The sources included David’s reign and his might.
easy.q: What did these sources describe about David?

answers: David, Israel, and the kingdoms of the countries
easy.explanation: The records also included Israel and all the kingdoms of the countries.
easy.q: Whom and what else did the records concern?

answers: They were sources who recorded or reported David’s acts
medium.explanation: The acts of David were written in the books associated with these three men.
medium.q: What role did Samuel, Nathan, and Gad have according to the passage?
Which word identifies Samuel as one who saw or received revelation?

answers: The account draws on records describing David and Israel
The records have no connection to the account
medium.explanation: The conclusion points to written sources for David’s acts, reign, and might.
medium.q: What is the relationship between these records and the account of David?

answers: To show that the sources covered periods and events throughout the reign
To say that no events occurred
To describe only David’s final day
challenge.explanation: The records included the various times and events that affected David and Israel.
challenge.q: Why does the passage mention “the times that went over” David and Israel?

answers: David’s reign was connected with wider historical events
The sources concerned only the Temple
challenge.explanation: The passage expands its scope to all the kingdoms of the countries.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the inclusion of other kingdoms?

answers: David’s reign and might were preserved in written historical records
It cancels the account of David’s reign
challenge.explanation: The closing verses connect David’s reign, might, and times with recorded sources.
challenge.q: What idea does the chapter’s conclusion reinforce?
